Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth! 6 And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell. 7 For every kind of beasts, and of birds, and of serpents, and of things in the sea, is tamed, and hath been tamed of mankind: 8 But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison. 9 Therewith bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the similitude of God. 10 Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be. (James 3:5-10 KJV)

These are such powerful scriptures, and it lets us know how deadly our tongues are. Most people don’t ever think about what they say, and just say things they don’t mean. Our tongue gets us into more trouble than our actions normally do, and if we could just control what we say, then we would get into much less trouble. The perfect man is the mature Christian that controls what he says (James 3:2). We should not ever speak negative things about anyone, not to them or behind their backs. Our words either speak life or death (Proverbs 18:21), and if you don’t speak life, then you are speaking death. There are no unimportant words, and Jesus said we would be held accountable for every idle word we speak (Matthew 12:36-37).

If we would keep in mind that God spoke this whole world into existence by His words (Genesis 1), and all that is on or in this world, so we need to understand the power that words have, as we are made in His image (Genesis 1:26). If we would watch what we say, and make a habit of listening a lot more then talking, we would learn a lot more. My daddy was a quiet person, and when asked why he was so quiet, he always said, “you don’t learn anything when you are talking”. We should all watch our words all the time, and speak only positive things, as you will end up eating the words that you say (Proverbs 18:20). Watch what you say at all times, letting the love of God flow through you to others.
